column1: # The checks of shell/control-text.nsh. See check-shell-log.sh.
# show-ifr shows the control characters, the Bidi_Control character and U+2028 of the prompts
# escaped, P04's backslash doubled and H05's line break inside its line. Raw, a terminal would
# take ESC[2J and U+009B as commands, U+202E as a reordering of the text and the line breaks as
# lines of their own; on the console, check-shell-log.sh deletes the control sequences and CR.
# A console whose TestString() takes U+010D and U+200D, such as OVMF's VT-UTF8 terminal, shows
# them as they are; on one that refuses them, such as a VT100 or PC-ANSI terminal of
# edk2-stable202608 TerminalDxe, uefisettings shows them escaped, as \u{10d} and \u{200d}.
# Raw there, each would reach the terminal as its low byte, CR, which check-shell-log.sh
# deletes, leaving P07<>Q and P08<>Q. The P08 checks hold U+200D, which shows as nothing.
# JSON escapes U+009B and U+202E, which it would carry raw, and jq reads the very prompts. A
# bracketed backslash, [\], is literal in an extended regular expression.

column3: any(.[]; .name == "P02<" + ([155] | implode) + ">Q") and any(.[]; .name == "P03<" + ([8238] | implode) + ">Q") and any(.[]; .name == "P06<" + ([8232] | implode) + ">Q") and any(.[]; .name == "P07<" + ([269] | implode) + ">Q") and any(.[]; .name == "P08<" + ([8205] | implode) + ">Q")
